request.query: In an Archimedean linear ordered field with FloorRing, finitely many positive weights have arbitrarily large natural multiples balanced within any positive relative error.

      "informal_name": "Existence of Approximating Indices for Admissible Absolute Values",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} (n : ℕ) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) {ε : ℝ},\n  0 < ε →\n    ∀ {b : R},\n      b ≠ 0 →\n        ∀ (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ n).succ → Fin n → R),\n          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : Fin n), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε",

items.informal_name: Existence of Integer Approximations for Real Numbers with Bounded Denominator
items.informal_description: For any real number $\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exist integers $j$ and $k$ such that $0 < k \leq n$ and $|k\xi - j| \leq \frac{1}{n + 1}$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Natural Number Between a*x and b*x for Large x
items.type: ∀ {a b : ℝ}, a < b → 0 ≤ b → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, a * x ≤ ↑n ∧ ↑n ≤ b * x
items.informal_description: For real numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfying $a < b$ and $0 \leq b$, there exists a real number $x_0$ such that for all $x \geq x_0$, there exists a natural number $n$ with $a x \leq n \leq b x$.

items.informal_name: Existence of a Natural Number with Bounded Diophantine Approximation
items.informal_description: For any real number $\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exists a natural number $k$ satisfying $1 \leq k \leq n$ such that the absolute difference between $k\xi$ and the nearest integer is at most $\frac{1}{n + 1}$, i.e., $\left| k\xi - \text{round}(k\xi) \right| \leq \frac{1}{n + 1}$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Approximating Indices for Admissible Absolute Values
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} (n : ℕ) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : R},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ n).succ → Fin n → R),
          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : Fin n), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, admissible absolute value $\abv$, positive real $\varepsilon$, nonzero element $b \in R$, and function $A : \mathrm{Fin}(\abv.\mathrm{card}(\varepsilon)^n + 1) \times \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to R$, there exist distinct indices $i_0, i_1$ such that for all $k$, the absolute value of $A(i_1, k) \bmod b - A(i_0, k) \bmod b$ is less than $\abv(b) \cdot \varepsilon$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Integers Between Scaled Reals for Large x
items.type: ∀ {a b : ℝ}, a < b → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, a * x ≤ ↑n ∧ ↑n ≤ b * x
items.informal_description: For any real numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a < b$, there exists a real number $x_0$ such that for all $x \geq x_0$, there exists an integer $n$ satisfying $a x \leq n \leq b x$.

items.informal_name: Projection of $ a + n\delta $ into $[a, b]$ Equals $ b $ for Large $ n $
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup α] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) {δ : α}
  [Archimedean α], 0 < δ → ∃ m, ∀ n ≥ m, ↑(Set.Icc.addNSMul h δ n) = b
items.informal_description: In an Archimedean ordered set $\alpha$, for any closed interval $[a, b]$ and any positive element $\delta$, there exists a natural number $m$ such that for all $n \geq m$, the projection of $a + n\delta$ into $[a, b]$ (defined as $\max(a, \min(b, a + n\delta))$) equals $b$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Rational Number Between Two Elements in Archimedean Ordered Field
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u_4} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] [Archimedean K] {x y : K} {n : ℕ},
  x < y → (y - x)⁻¹ < ↑n → ∃ z, x < ↑z / ↑n ∧ ↑z / ↑n < y
items.informal_description: For any elements $x$ and $y$ in an Archimedean ordered field $K$ with $x < y$, and for any natural number $n$ satisfying $\frac{1}{y - x} < n$, there exists an integer $z$ such that $x < \frac{z}{n} < y$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Approximate Solutions under Admissible Absolute Values
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : R},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (h : abv.IsAdmissible) (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ Fintype.card ι).succ → ι → R),
          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : ι), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε
items.informal_description: For any finite set $\iota$, positive real number $\varepsilon$, non-zero element $b$ in a Euclidean domain $R$ equipped with an admissible absolute value, and a function $A : \text{Fin}(N) \to \iota \to R$ (where $N = (\text{card}(\varepsilon)^{\#\iota} + 1)$), there exist distinct indices $i_0$ and $i_1$ such that for all $k$, the absolute value of the difference between the remainders $A(i_1, k) \bmod b$ and $A(i_0, k) \bmod b$ is strictly less than $\varepsilon \cdot |b|$. This result leverages the pigeonhole principle and properties of admissible absolute values compatible with the Euclidean division algorithm.
